transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

I guess what brings me in is... well, I got really worked up in a staff meeting the other day. I started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill, you know? Like, moving chairs around, waving my arms everywhere, really getting into it. And I couldn't seem to stop, even when folks told me to sit down. It was just... I had to show them. You know, working as a personal care aide, falls are a big deal. My buddy Dave, he slipped on some ice last winter—not at work, just outside his apartment—and he broke his collarbone. He was out of work for weeks, and his dog, this little terrier mix, got so anxious with him just sitting around in a sling. I used to go over and walk the dog for him. Buster, that was his name. Good dog, but he pulled on the leash like you wouldn't believe. Anyway, yeah, the meeting... they said I was being disruptive.
How has your sleep been lately?

Sleep? Oh, well... I've been sleeping maybe two, three hours a night. I'll wake up way before dawn, and honestly, I feel completely fine. Ready to go, you know? I don't see the problem with being up while the house is still dark, just... making plans, getting things organized. It's actually really quiet then. The streetlights outside my window have this weird orange glow, and sometimes I watch the moths bumping against the glass. There was this one moth last week, huge thing, looked almost like a bat. Reminded me of when I went camping with my uncle when I was a kid. We pitched this tent out by Lake George, and the mosquitoes were just eating us alive. He had this citronella candle that smelled like burnt lemon, and we tried to make s'mores, but the marshmallows kept catching on fire. I always liked mine a little charred anyway. But yeah, I wake up early, feel great, and just start planning out my day.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt the complete opposite—feeling deeply down, depressed, or having very low energy for weeks at a time?

Down? No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had days where I didn't want to go into work, but who hasn't, right? Especially when Mrs. Higgins is on the schedule. She's this client I had, real sweet lady most of the time, but she insisted on watching these old black-and-white westerns all afternoon. The volume had to be all the way up because her hearing aids were always acting up. I tried telling her daughter about getting them checked, but the daughter lives out in Ohio somewhere. Cleveland, I think. Or maybe Columbus. I had a buddy who moved to Columbus for a girl, and they ended up breaking up before he even unpacked his boxes. He had to drive a U-Haul all the way back in a snowstorm. Have you ever driven a U-Haul? They handle like a boat, just swaying all over the highway. But yeah, no, I don't really get down like that. I just keep moving.
Have you been taking any recreational drugs, new medications, or stimulants lately?

Drugs? No, no, I don't mess with any of that stuff. No new medications either. I mean, I drink coffee, if that counts as a stimulant? Though lately I haven't even really needed it. I used to drink those huge energy drinks, though, you know, the ones in the tall black cans with the bright green claw marks on them? My buddy Dave—the one with Buster, the dog I was telling you about—he used to drink like four of those a day when we were working third shift at this auto parts warehouse a few years back. 

That place was freezing, man. They kept the giant shipping bay doors open even in November, and the wind would just whip right through the aisles. I had to wear these thick thermal socks, the heavy wool ones my Aunt Carol got me for Christmas. She knits them herself, which is real nice of her, but she uses the scratchiest yarn you've ever felt in your life. You have to wash them like three or four times with extra fabric softener before you can even put them on your feet without going crazy. And fabric softener is getting so expensive now, have you noticed? I was at the grocery store on Tuesday and a regular bottle was almost ten bucks. It's just soap for your clothes, it shouldn't cost that much. But yeah, no, no drugs or anything like that for me.
Have you ever had another period in your life where you felt this energized and needed very little sleep, or is this the first time?

Well, I mean, it's not the first time. I've had these... stretches, I guess you'd call them. Where I'm just totally wired, full of energy, barely sleeping, and I've got all these big plans going on. It's been happening off and on for, I don't know, about 11 months now? 

It actually started right around the time I decided I was going to build that deck in the backyard. I bought all this treated lumber, stacked it up by the fence. It's still out there, actually. You know, you really have to watch out for termites with that wood if it sits too long. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he had termites get into his garage a couple years ago. They had to tent the whole thing, big red and yellow striped tent, looked like a circus was in town. He was so mad because he had to move his vintage Corvette out into the driveway for three days. Beautiful car, cherry red, 1969. I always wanted a classic car, maybe a Mustang. But anyway, yeah, these energized periods, they've been coming and going for almost a year now.
